3.2.2 System 2: Speculative Verification and Memory Consolidation
Inspired by speculative decoding’s acceptance rule (Leviathan et al., 2023; Chen et al., 2023a), System 2’s binary policy πver θ assesses whether selected chunks warrant memory updates.
For candidate indices It = {i | ci ∈Ct}, the action-level acceptance probability is
αt,i = min(1, πver θ(Update | q, ci, mt) / πsel ϕ(Update | q, ci, mt)). (4)
Independently draw ξt,i ∼U(0, 1) for each candidate and accept it if ξt,i ≤αt,i.
If any candidate is accepted, commit the first accepted chunk in document order and generate its replacement memory:
mt+1 ∼πmem θ (· | q, ci⋆ t , mt), (5)
where i⋆ t = min{i ∈It | ξt,i ≤αt,i}.
As a special case, if no candidate is accepted, retain the current memory and advance past the window.
Otherwise, discard remaining predictions conditioned on mt and resume immediately after the committed chunk with mt+1.
Answering uses the query and final memory; Algorithm 3 in Appendix B.4 gives the complete transitions.
3.3 Training of MemDuet
Figure 3 summarizes three-stage training.
Stage I trains memory-conditioned evidence selection.
Stage II freezes System 1 and trains System 2 to verify candidates, rewrite memory, and generate answers.
Stage III jointly optimizes both systems with task rewards, coordinating selection with verification and memory updates.
3.3.1 Stage I: System 1 Supervised Warm-up
We initialize System 1 on HotpotQA (Yang et al., 2018) by aligning gold supporting facts with document chunks.
Evidence-containing chunks are labeled Update, and other chunks Skip.

We retain the original example and add a postupdate negative:
(q, c, m) −→ Update, (q, c, m′) −→ Skip. (6)
We train on the original examples and post-update negatives using the memory-contrastive objective:
LStage I(ϕ) = LwCE + λpair Lpair, Lpair = EP[max(0, γ − ∆sϕ)]. (7)
Here, LwCE is class-weighted action cross-entropy; P contains matched memory pairs, with ∆sϕ = sϕ(q, c, m) −sϕ(q, c, m′).
The score sϕ is the UPDATE-minus-SKIP logit difference, and γ is the margin.
Hyperparameters are reported in Appendix B.1.
